user:
Research problem: In MVFA's zero-shot (leave-one-modality-out) training, the segmentation adapters — the only part that produces anomaly maps — are trained with Dice and Focal losses exclusively on the three source datasets that have pixel masks (BrainMRI, LiverCT, RESC), while OCT17, ChestXray and HIS only train the detection adapters. Primary question: can the segmentation adapters be trained from image-level labels alone, and how much mask-supervised localisation does that retain on the unseen modality? At each of the four adapter levels, with the original level weights, the Dice and Focal terms are replaced by an image-level BCE on the top-k mean of the level's patch-to-text anomaly probabilities (k = 1% of patches), applied to all five source datasets with every mask discarded; the detection adapters and their loss are unchanged. Hypothesis: because patch scores are similarities to text anchors shared by all modalities, this weak supervision yields localisation that transfers to the unseen modality. Primary outcomes: pixel-level AUROC and AUPRO on the held-out folds with masks (BrainMRI, LiverCT, RESC) and image-level AUROC on all folds, mask-supervised versus image-label-supervised MVFA under the shared protocol. Secondary analyses: (i) a control in which the text anchors of the segmentation branch are replaced by a learned linear patch classifier trained with the same MIL loss, isolating the role of the text anchors; (ii) a per-level breakdown; (iii) two label-budget points with masks for 10% and 25% of the abnormal source images (one seed, two folds).

Below are 24 candidate research ideas for this problem. Group them into 4-7 method families such that ideas in the same family share their core mechanism (not merely their goal). Give each family a short name.

[A1-g0-C1] Asymmetric sigmoid MIL for mask-free MVFA segmentation adapters
Train MVFA's segmentation adapters from image labels only: every patch of a normal image is pushed to the normal anchor and the top-1% patches of an abnormal image to the abnormal anchor, with a SigLIP-style sigmoid loss at all four levels.

[A1-g0-C2] MIL-to-mask self-distillation with cross-level agreement
First train the segmentation adapters with the problem's top-k MIL, then convert their multi-level maps on abnormal source images into pseudo-masks (patches anomalous at three or more levels) and retrain with MVFA's Dice and Focal losses on those pseudo-masks.

[A1-g0-C3] DINOv2-affinity propagation of MIL evidence into pseudo-masks
Refine the MIL-trained patch maps of abnormal source images by propagation over a frozen DINOv2 patch-affinity graph and use the result as pseudo-masks for MVFA's Dice and Focal losses.

[A1-g0-C4] Hybrid supervision: synthetic-lesion masks plus real-image MIL
Train the segmentation adapters with Dice + Focal on synthetic lesions pasted into normal source images and with the problem's top-k MIL on real image-labelled abnormal images, never loading an expert mask.

[A1-g0-C5] Anatomy-debiased MIL: normal hard negatives and a positional normal prior
Make the problem's top-k MIL pick lesions rather than anatomy by (i) penalising the top-k patches of normal images and (ii) ranking abnormal-image patches after subtracting a running per-position mean of normal-image scores of the same dataset.

[A1-g0-C6] Is it the words or the frame? Anchor controls for MIL-trained segmentation adapters
Train the segmentation adapters with the problem's top-k MIL against three references — MVFA's text anchors, scale-matched random anchors, and a learned linear patch head — and test which property (meaning, fixed frame, scale) drives transfer of weakly supervised localisation.

[A1-g1-o1] Cross-level consensus MIL: choosing instances by agreement of the four adapter levels
Select the positive instances of an abnormal image as the patches on which all four segmentation levels agree (geometric mean of level probabilities) and apply the MIL loss to those patches at every level, in a single training stage.

[A1-g1-o2] Normal-bank-gated MIL: selecting abnormal instances by distance to normal source patches
Replace the positional normal prior of anatomy-debiased MIL with a feature-space prior: rank the patches of an abnormal image by anomaly probability times their distance to a bank of normal patches of the same source dataset, so salient but normal anatomy is not selected — without assuming spatial alignment.

[A1-g1-o3] Equivariance-regularised MIL: dense self-supervision from geometric transforms
Densify the sparse MIL signal by requiring the segmentation maps of an image and of its flipped/rotated/cropped copy to agree after inverse transformation, using no pseudo-masks and no extra backbone.

[A1-g1-o4] Counterfactual occlusion targets: teaching the segmentation adapters what the image-label detector needs
Use MVFA's image-label-trained detection branch as a counterfactual oracle: the patches whose occlusion (replacement by matched normal tissue) most lowers its image score form the training target of the segmentation adapters, so localisation is learned from causal evidence rather than from the highest-scoring patches.

[A1-g1-o5] Anatomy-debiased MIL under text and random anchor frames
Train the segmentation adapters with top-k MIL plus hard-negative mining of the top-k patches of normal images, under MVFA's text anchors and under scale-matched random anchors, to test both whether debiasing improves weak localisation and whether its effect depends on the meaning of the anchors.

[A1-g1-o6] Witness-rate-adaptive MIL: estimating each dataset's lesion fraction by positive-unlabelled mixture-proportion estimation
Replace the fixed k = 1% of the MIL operator by a per-dataset witness rate estimated from image labels alone — the fraction of patches in abnormal images whose scores are not explained by the normal-image score distribution — and update it during training.

[A1-g2-o1] Matched-pair MIL ranking: borrowing the ranking objective of weakly supervised video anomaly detection
Train the segmentation adapters with a ranking loss that requires the most anomalous patches of an abnormal image to score above the most anomalous patches of its most similar normal image from the same dataset, instead of pushing absolute probabilities to 0 and 1.

[A1-g2-o2] Mosaic MIL: free quadrant labels from four-image mosaics
Create training mosaics of four down-scaled source images (normal and abnormal, same dataset) whose quadrant labels are known from the image labels, and train the segmentation adapters to localise abnormality at quadrant level together with consensus MIL inside abnormal quadrants.

[A1-g2-o3] Consensus MIL with an anchor-frame control
Train the segmentation adapters with cross-level consensus MIL under MVFA's text anchors and under scale-matched random anchors, testing whether consensus selection improves weak localisation and whether its benefit relies on the shared anchor frame rather than on the anchors' meaning.

[A1-g2-o4] Posterior-weighted MIL: a two-component mixture of patch scores replaces hard top-k selection
Keep the witness-rate framing but replace hard top-k selection with soft per-patch weights: a two-component mixture fitted per dataset on patch scores, with the normal component fixed from normal images, gives every patch of an abnormal image a posterior probability of being lesion, used as its target weight.

[A1-g2-o5] Co-teaching MIL between MVFA's detection and segmentation adapters
Let MVFA's two adapter sets select instances for each other: the detection branch's patch map (trained on all images with image labels) chooses the top-k patches on which the segmentation branch's MIL loss is applied, and vice versa, so neither branch reinforces its own spurious maxima.

[A1-g2-o6] Distilling a normal-bank novelty map into the segmentation adapters alongside MIL
Give the segmentation adapters a dense, label-free auxiliary target on every source image — the distance of each patch to a bank of normal patches of the same dataset — and combine it with image-level MIL, so localisation is shaped everywhere rather than only at the top-k.

[A1-g3-o1] Learnable log-sum-exp pooling per dataset replaces fixed top-k in MIL
Replace the hard top-k mean of the MIL operator by log-sum-exp pooling with a learnable temperature per source dataset, which interpolates smoothly between max and mean pooling and lets gradient descent find each dataset's effective lesion fraction from image labels.

[A1-g3-o2] Per-image adaptive k from normal-bank exceedances
Set the MIL instance count of each abnormal image to the number of its patches whose distance to a bank of normal patches of the same dataset exceeds the 99th percentile of normal-image distances, so k follows the lesion size of that image rather than a fixed or per-dataset value.

[A1-g3-o3] Mosaic MIL with normal-bank-gated instance selection
Train the segmentation adapters on four-image mosaics whose normal quadrants are pixel-level negatives, and select the positive instances inside abnormal quadrants by anomaly probability gated by distance to a normal-patch bank, so both the spatial contrast and the instance choice avoid normal anatomy.

[A1-g3-o4] Mosaic-to-single-image map consistency
Keep the mosaic framing but replace the label-proportion (mass) consistency with dense map consistency: the segmentation map of each quadrant of a mosaic must equal the map of its source image computed alone at the same resolution.

[A1-g3-o5] MPE-anchored posterior MIL
Fix the mixing proportion of the posterior-weighted MIL mixture to the witness rate estimated by positive-unlabelled mixture-proportion estimation, and fit only the lesion component, which makes the per-patch posteriors stable early in training while keeping soft targets.

[A1-g3-o6] Feature-space anomaly mixing: graded synthetic positives from normal-bank patches
Create synthetic training patches in feature space by mixing the features of normal-bank patches with those of the gated top patches of abnormal images at random ratios, and train the segmentation adapters to output the mixing ratio, giving dense, graded patch-level supervision without image-space artefacts.
